output.briefing:
This direction concerns only the explicit family dkp_square_family(t), not an exhaustive parametrization of Diophantine sextuples. Its target is to prove that, for every rational t outside {0,1,-1}, none of the six coordinates is an integer. Write d=t^2-1, h=t^2+1, and v=t^4+34t^2+1. The exact coordinates are a=-9h/(8d), b=(t^2-7)h(7t^2-1)/(8d^3), c=8d^3/(9h^3), e=-2(t^2+5)(5t^2+1)/(9dh), f=-2t(t^2-4t-3)(3t^2-4t-1)(t^3+8t^2+5t+4)(4t^3-5t^2+8t-1)/(dhv^2), and g=2t(t^2+4t-3)(3t^2+4t-1)(t^3-8t^2+5t-4)(4t^3+5t^2+8t+1)/(dhv^2). For this target domain, write t=m/n in lowest terms with n>0; then m≠0 and m^2≠n^2. All displayed denominators are nonzero. The definition itself allows t=0, where f=g=0, but that parameter is excluded from the target claim.

A complete partial result follows directly from the displayed formula: c is nonzero and nonintegral throughout the target domain. Indeed, |c|=(8/9)|d|^3/h^3, and |t^2-1|<t^2+1 for rational t, so 0<|c|<8/9. Preserve the cube in this identity; it is not (8/9)|d/h|. This establishes only the assertion for coordinate c, not the family claim that all six coordinates are nonintegers.

For a,b,e, the proposal suggests negative 2-adic valuations for a,b and that integrality of e might force H|32, with H=m^2+n^2 and D=m^2-n^2. These are unproved suggestions: derive reduced numerator/denominator conditions and establish each implication, including parity cases and cancellations. For f,g, set Q=m^4+34m^2n^2+n^4. Any use of polynomial gcd/Bezout arguments against q(T)=T^4+34T^2+1 needs explicit identities or certificates. The proposal reports candidate resultants 1, 18432, 18432, 1492992, 1492992 for the factors T, T^2-4T-3, 3T^2-4T-1, T^3+8T^2+5T+4, 4T^3-5T^2+8T-1, respectively; these are unverified hints, not established lemmas. Prove any implication that integrality forces Q to have prime support only at 2 and 3, determine exact v2(Q) and v3(Q) cases, and justify the comparison with Q>36. Check t↦-t and its exact effect on f,g, and handle vanishing factors, signs, exceptional parameters, and every possible cancellation.

The proposal is not a proof and the auxiliary all-height claim remains open on this record. Give either a complete proof of that claim or the strongest fully proved, correctly quantified partial theorem, explicitly identifying remaining cases. Finite searches do not settle unbounded rational height. Even a proof excluding this family would not decide the locked existence question: both unrestricted-sign and all-positive cases remain open, and no exhaustiveness link to the family is established. Do not promote prior experiments or suggested resultants to accepted results. The snapshot records no attempts, reviews, or reusable lemmas.
uncertainties: The all-height nonintegrality claim for all six coordinates remains unproved. Valuation and divisibility implications, the proposed H|32 step, any Bezout certificates, Q prime support and local valuation cases, and exceptional/cancellation cases for f and g all need proof.
The candidate resultant values in the proposal are not independently verified and cannot be treated as established identities.
Neither the auxiliary family claim nor the proved partial result for c decides the main problem's unrestricted-sign or all-positive existence cases.

assumptions: All six elements are nonzero rational numbers and pairwise distinct.
At least two elements are integers.
Each of the fifteen pairwise products plus one is a rational square; zero square roots are allowed.
quantifiers: Existentially over all six-element rational sets, with no bound on rational height or integer anchors.
A nonexistence argument must cover every allowable set and every integer-anchor pair.
problem_contract.statement: Determine whether there exists a set of six pairwise distinct nonzero rational numbers containing at least two integers, with xy+1 a rational square for every distinct pair. Track the all-positive and unrestricted-sign cases separately. Auxiliary construction-family exclusions are partial results and do not decide the main question.
